name: Beta admin — export all data (JSON download)
gap: Export a backup writes one real JSON file through <a download> with everything LKStore.dump() holds, plus the schema version and the per-key change stamps a restore needs to merge. v6's beta-admin half — four beta collections (activity log, tester roster, two counters) — is not reproduced and will not be: those are an operator's view of other people's usage, they do not exist as keys in this build, and the reason is written into the export row's own source.
evidence: drove it — the downloaded file parses, carries 31 lk_ keys under data and a stamps map, and restores back into the store

name: Beta admin — "Sync All to Server Now"
gap: Cut, with the reason written above syncRow() in settings.html. Sync now is the same action with a better rule (LKCloud.push sends what changed since the last sync, pull takes what changed on the other side); a second button beside it whose only difference is "ignore the change stamps" is an operator's tool in a consumer screen. Forcing a full push would also need an API cloud.js does not expose, and cloud.js belongs to another package.

name: Notification preference — Rest timer
gap: The preference is built, stored in lk_notifPrefs and survives a reload, and the row says the moment it would fire ("The moment the timer runs out."). Still needed: a push subscription and a server to send from — a service worker can show a notification but only a push wakes it. The card says exactly that under the switches, and turning one on says it again.
evidence: drove it — toggled, reloaded, still off

name: Notification preference — Training day + send time
gap: The preference and its OWN send time are built: the switch writes lk_reminderOn, the Send at row under it writes lk_reminderAt, and moving it no longer moves the check-in. The duplicate workout switch in the Reminders card is gone, so there is one control over one key. Still needed: a push subscription and a sender.
evidence: drove it — set to 6:30 AM, lk_reminderAt is "06:30", survives a reload, lk_notifTimes.checkin unchanged

name: Notification preference — Daily check-in + send time
gap: The preference and its own send time are built; the time is lk_notifTimes.checkin, separate from the workout reminder's. Still needed: a push subscription and a sender.
evidence: drove it — set to 8:00 PM, lk_notifTimes = {checkin:"20:00"}, survives a reload

name: Notification preference — Unfinished workout
gap: Built. It is event-driven rather than a time of day, so the row says when instead of offering a clock: "Two hours after the last set you logged." Still needed: a push subscription and a sender.
evidence: drove it — switch-notif-unfinished stores under lk_notifPrefs and survives a reload

name: Notification preference — Supplements
gap: Built, and the row now says where its time comes from rather than leaving it implied: "At the time of day each one is set to, under Fuel." Still needed: a push subscription and a sender.

name: Notification preference — Compounds
gap: Built. It starts off and cannot be armed while Stack tracking is off — the row says so rather than offering a preference with no subject — and its time comes from the cycle in Stack. Still needed: a push subscription and a sender.
evidence: drove it — the switch is disabled and explained until lk_perfTracking is on

name: Notification preference — Restock
gap: Built, with its own send time in lk_notifTimes.restock. Still needed: a push subscription and a sender.
evidence: drove it — toggled off, reloaded, still off; time stored separately from the other two

name: About Me — Height (cm, or ft + in)
evidence: drove it — on pounds the sheet takes feet and inches; 5 ft 10 in stores lk_profile.heightCm = 178 and reads back as 178 cm after switching to kilograms

name: Daily check-in frequency (1 / 2 / 4 per day)
evidence: drove it — the row offers Once / Twice / Four times and writes lk_checkinPerDay 1 / 2 / 4, the three values coach.html's checkinPerDay() accepts; Off is gone from this row because it wrote a 0 the coach reads back as 1, and whether the app says anything is the Daily check-in notification switch

name: Fuel display settings card (hide numbers, dashboard framing)
gap: "Show calorie numbers" is here and Fuel honours it (fuel.html reads lk_fuelNumbers). The Left/Eaten dashboard framing is deliberately not here: fuel.html reads no framing key, so a switch on this screen would be a control that does nothing, and the reason is written into seenSection()'s source. If it is wanted it belongs in fuel.html, which this package does not own.

name: Nutrition CSV / JSON export and full-account backup/restore
evidence: drove it — the CSV now carries a weigh-in table (lk_weightLog, and lk_bfLog where there is one) under the meals and targets; the backup carries the per-key change stamps; Restore asks Merge (keeping whichever copy is newer, by the same stamps cloud.js merges on) or Replace, and the merge kept the newer local key and took the newer file key, saying which in the toast

name: Cycle-tracking opt-in sync
gap: The Settings half is built: a Back up your cycle log switch under Cycle tracking, writing lk_mcProfile.cloudBackup — the field cloud.js already gates lk_mcProfile, lk_mcDays and lk_mcFuelAdjust on, in both directions — naming exactly which records it governs and saying plainly that nothing has been uploaded either way because there is no server. One key, two surfaces: the Cycle screen's own switch writes the same field. Still needed: the Supabase deploy, after which the switch decides what a sync may carry.
evidence: drove it — the switch appears only when cycle tracking is on, writes lk_mcProfile.cloudBackup = true and survives a reload

name: Deploy-version check / cache bust
gap: No backend is needed and none is used: the version is the service worker's own cache name (assemble.mjs writes locked-<byte length> into sw.js), fetched from the worker's registered scriptURL with cache: 'no-store', so any static host that publishes the app publishes its version. Opened from a file, or served with no worker, the row says there is nothing to check against rather than claiming to be up to date.
where: settings.html checkVersion(), checkServiceWorker(), versionRow(), updateBanner(), forceRefresh()
evidence: drove it — with a worker registered the row reads "Build 111. Up to date."; republishing as 222 raises a banner naming both builds, and Reload into the new version writes lk_deployVersion = 222, clears Cache Storage, reloads, and the banner is gone

name: Service worker registration
gap: The worker is generated and registered by 10-final/assemble.mjs, which this package does not own. What was missing here was the truth about it: Settings said "this build has none" after one had been added. It now reads the registration and says which of the four states it is in, the test send goes through the worker where there is one, and the card says what a worker still cannot do — a notification that arrives while the app is closed needs a push subscription and a server to send it, and there is neither.
evidence: drove it — with a worker registered the card reads "A service worker is running…", the test send goes through registration.showNotification and reports failure honestly when the browser refuses

name: Deploy-version check and cache bust
gap: Same mechanism as F-SYNC-005: checked on load, again on every lk:enter, and on demand from the App version row; the bust is Force refresh, which clears Cache Storage and reloads, and records the version it is reloading into so the banner cannot come back for a build already running.

name: Deploy-version cache bust
gap: Closed by the same code as F-SYNC-005 and F-SYS-004, with lk_deployVersion as the stored comparison. Nothing reloads by itself: a build swapped under somebody mid-set loses the set, so the check tells them and they choose.
